findings.title: Knowledge is not auto-wired into any runtime bootstrap
findings.detail: 0 hits across 150 scanned runtime files → integration verified on demand only; automatic wiring still pending authorization
findings.impact: The agent does not pick up the curriculum on its own. Integration is proven by direct invocation (M1-M6, S1-S3), not by a running service.
findings.recommendation: Separate authorized change: call kb.ingestInto(memoryFabric) once at bootstrap (idempotent - M6) and register kb.toSkillCandidates() with the skills registry.

findings.title: Promoted knowledge skills are not durable
findings.detail: fresh SkillsRegistry returns null=true; memory-fabric records still durable=73 → recommendation: persist promoted knowledge skills via memory-fabric 'skill' type or mission-ledger
findings.impact: A restart loses every promoted skill; only memory-fabric records survive (M3).
findings.recommendation: Persist promoted skills as memory-fabric 'skill' records or in the mission ledger.

findings.title: memory-fabric hash embeddings rank knowledge weakly
findings.detail: found 5/5 probed records; top-3 hits=1/5 (hash embedding fallback)
findings.impact: Every lesson is retrievable (5/5) but only 1/5 probes land in the top 3; ranks observed: [1, 8, 7, 13, 7]
findings.recommendation: Use /api/v1/knowledge/search (lexical + IDF, 8/8 top-1 in A7) as the ranking surface; upgrade embeddings to nomic-embed-text via Ollama for vector ranking.

findings.title: Quiz answer positions are guessable (content authoring, not an API leak)
findings.detail: always picking index 1 would score 76.9% (20/26 quizzes); distribution={0: 3, 1: 20, 2: 2, 3: 1}; longest same-index streak=5. Recommendation: shuffle option order per quiz (authoring-side change, not an API change).
findings.impact: Always choosing index 1 scores 76.9% without reading the lesson.
findings.recommendation: Shuffle option order per quiz in curriculum.json and update answerIndex (authoring change; the API already hides the key - A5/A6 PASS).

findings.title: package-lock.json did not contain the new workspace package
findings.detail: npm install added node_modules/@agi-system/knowledge + packages/knowledge to the lockfile (8 lines). Without it, `npm ci` would not link the workspace package.
findings.impact: CI installs would not resolve @agi-system/knowledge; tests only passed via the vitest alias.
findings.recommendation: Commit the lockfile update together with the audit commit.

findings.title: Lexical search matches sub-tokens of nonsense queries
findings.detail: The query 'zzzqqq-no-such-token' returned 2 hits because 'token' is a real curriculum term; a token with no real substring returns 0 hits.
findings.impact: None - expected lexical behaviour; documented so the audit does not mistake it for a leak.

conditions: Push the audit commit and open the PR from arena/01a0c57e-12pro so the evidence is public.
The /learn UI must be read-path only (API endpoints verified in G5/G5b). Automatic runtime ingestion stays a separate, explicitly authorized change (FINDING-1).
Ranking in the UI must come from /api/v1/knowledge/search (lexical+IDF). Do not rank with memory-fabric vector top-k until embeddings are upgraded (FINDING-3).
Quizzes may be shown for practice, but must not be presented as an assessment or scored publicly until option order is shuffled (FINDING-4).
UI copy must not claim durable skill learning: promoted skills live in memory only (FINDING-2).
Include the package-lock.json workspace entry (FINDING-5) in the commit.
decision.rationale: All 10 audit steps produced machine-readable evidence and no gate failed. The chain Knowledge → Loader → Retrieval → API → Memory Fabric → Skills Registry is verified against the real collaborators (not mocks), the API is proven to serve the authored files byte-for-byte, and no answer-key material leaves the grading path. Remaining items are disclosed findings with explicit conditions, not unknowns.
